$comment: Pipeline parameters. Source bindings, thresholds and detection rules live here so the code carries no domain values and no magic numbers. Dimension derivations live in dimensions.json. See docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md.

snapshot.$comment: A first-registration month is the snapshot month only if it holds at least this share of the median of the months before it (trailing_window_months of them). A few rows dated after the register's own month are then not mistaken for the next snapshot. The lowest real month on record, 2020-04, held 7% of its trailing median (measured on the 2026-10 snapshot).

schedule.$comment: From this day of the month (UTC) a run that builds nothing fails if the previous month's snapshot is still not built (docs/DATA_SOURCES.md, Refresh timing).

run_summary.$comment: The order of a build's warnings on the Monthly build's summary page (pipeline/fetch.py order_warnings), worst first; any warning no group claims follows, in the order the build raised it. A group claims a warning whose text holds `contains`: the text is what the build already says, so the tests build each of these warnings and check which group claims it. The first is a flip of a dataset's mild hybrid split, which rewrites the dataset's whole history of two values; the second is an unmapped-value guard above its warning level, which stops a later build if it grows.

warning_order.label: Rewrites published history
warning_order.contains: Every month of the dataset's history changes

warning_order.label: Close to stopping a later build

vehicle.$also_comment: Wider scopes: a flag of `rows` (the key) that is true for a vehicle whose type is true in this column of the vehicle scope file and whose import status is in scope. A dataset names one scope flag in its `require` (`in_scope` or one of these) and counts the types that flag says (D-113).

hybrid_classification.$comment: mild_hybrid_models.csv: which hybrid nameplates are mild or full. Match columns are the model_registry_conditions above. See docs/METRICS.md for the coverage figure.
hybrid_classification.$split_comment: A dataset whose trailing high-confidence coverage is under publish_split_at_trailing_high_confidence_coverage does not publish the mild split: its mild hybrids are counted under undivided_powertrain (a value of the powertrain column), and its manifest says so (mild_split_published). Judged for each dataset by its own figure. Equal to the warning level today, so a dataset warns exactly when it withholds; the two may differ.

associations.$comment: How strongly each pair of a dataset's fact-table dimensions moves together (pipeline/association.py, docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md Associations): the bias-corrected Cramer's V, written to associations/{dataset}.json for the whole dataset and for the trailing_window_months, rounded to this many decimals. Which pairs are not findings comes from config/data_map.json.

registrations_surviving.$scope_comment: Counts the five vehicle types the vehicle scope file marks in its trade_scope column (in_trade_scope), the types of the wider scope, since D-157: the published split into light and heavy commercial holds buses, motor caravans and special purpose vehicles, which the default scope (in_scope) leaves out. in_scope is unchanged and is still read by the in-scope row count the guardrails compare with the last good build and by the event checks, so a deliberate change of this dataset's scope moves neither.
registrations_surviving.$pairs_comment: The two-dimensional slices this dataset emits, each [dim_a, dim_b], written to pairs/{dataset}/{dim_a}__{dim_b}.parquet. Only pairs a chart or filter needs (docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md, Pair slices).
registrations_surviving.$facts_comment: The fact table: counts by month and every dimension listed here, one Parquet file per column under facts/{dataset}/, so the browser can answer any combination by downloading only the columns a question needs (docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md, Fact table; D-058). region is left out on purpose (D-078), and the user's rule for owner fields allows them in a slice or a pair only (D-096): it is where the vehicle's owner lives, and with it two in three of the table's rows counted a single vehicle.
registrations_surviving.$narrow_facts_comment: Narrow fact tables (D-144, docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md, Narrow fact tables): a second, smaller table for a field that would make every question heavier as a column of the wide one. Each is written to facts/{dataset}/narrow/{id}/{column}.parquet with the wide table's rows, order and checks, and listed in the manifest under facts.narrow. A dimension that reads an owner field is refused here as in facts. colour was +75% of the wide table (D-116 item 6); with make and the powertrain in five groups it is 353,976 bytes on the 2026-10 pull (D-144 has the other sets measured).

fleet.$comment: A stock (D-135, docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md, Stock datasets): every vehicle in the register at the snapshot, of every vehicle type and every import status, counted as at the snapshot date, with one period, the snapshot's month. It is not a series of first registrations: no vehicle's month or year of first registration is a dimension of it or a column of any of its files, and the build refuses a dimension of it that reads one (not_by). `dimensions` lists the only dimensions it is offered: how the register records the vehicle's usage now (an owner field, so its slice and its pair are held to the small-cell rules), and the type NZTA registers the vehicle under. No fact table: a field that describes the owner never reaches one.

new_registrations.$comment: New registrations (D-158): every vehicle first registered in a month, new and used, of the five vehicle types the vehicle scope file marks in its trade_scope column (in_trade_scope), read from the supplied source nzta_dashboard through the same normalise, derive and output code as the register and with the same import-status rule (fleet_entry) as registrations_surviving, which counts the same five types since D-157. It replaces registrations_flow (two types) and registrations_flow_wider (five types, the same facts): vehicle type, and so the narrower scope, is a condition of a question, not a dataset. Both are retired in dimensions.json, so an older link still opens. The dashboard's RE-REG and SCRATCH rows are in the store and are not fleet entries. No pairs. Only dimensions the source carries are listed in facts: one it lacks (a dimension that needs the gross vehicle mass, engine size or district) would abort, not wait.
new_registrations.$continues_comment: The datasets whose place this one took, by id (D-158). The guards compare a dataset with the record the last good build kept under its own id; a dataset with none has nothing to be compared with on its first build, so a month the dashboard restated, a month emptied, a dimension that stopped being live or a mild hybrid split that flipped would pass once. A dataset listed here that has no record of its own takes the first listed id's record for that run (pipeline/guardrails.py, inherit_history). Only an id that counted the same vehicles belongs here: registrations_flow_wider counted this dataset's five types, registrations_flow counted two. An id still built as a dataset is refused.

registrations_cars_long_run.$comment: Read from the supplied source statsnz_tpt, a source of kind series (pipeline/series.py): Stats NZ's monthly count of cars and station wagons registered for the first time, from January 1961. `total` is the series that gives each month's vehicles. Its dimensions (car_origin, car_engine_band in dimensions.json) are Stats NZ's own breakdowns of that total, published separately, so they cannot be crossed with each other or with anything else: there are no pairs and no fact table. Nothing else the table holds (commercial vehicles, buses, motorcycles, power cycles, tractors) is built, because its classes are not lined up with NZTA's vehicle types (D-065).

supplied.$comment: Sources a maintainer supplies by hand as a CSV, checked and kept in a store by `python -m pipeline supply <id> <csv>` (pipeline/supplied.py). The Action never runs that command and nothing here is fetched. The store (a Parquet file of counts and a ledger) is committed to the repository (D-097), so a build on GitHub reads the same files as a local build. `fields` maps a logical field name of the top-level `fields` block to the CSV column that carries it; `extra_fields` are public columns the register does not have, kept in the store under the name given; `private_columns` must be in the header and are dropped, so the owner's district reaches neither the store nor any output. The two kind-of-owner columns (owner type and usage at registration, the data map's group kind_of_owner) are kept as extra_fields: they say what kind of owner registered a vehicle, not who or where, and the build keeps them apart from every field that says where the owner lives (pipeline/privacy.py). `publisher`, `licence`, `attribution` and `origin` are copied into the store's ledger each time `supply` writes it, so the committed file carries its own terms.

nzta_dashboard.attribution: Motor vehicle registrations dashboard open data, NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi, licensed CC BY 4.0. Counts of vehicles first registered in each month, with the kind of owner (owner type and usage at registration); the owner's district is not kept.
nzta_dashboard.origin: NZTA's registrations dashboard (the First registration report), exported by hand by the repository's owner and checked by `python -m pipeline supply`.
nzta_dashboard.$outside_scope_comment: For a row whose vehicle type and import status the named dataset does not count (its `require` flags, read from the scope files the build reads, with the vehicle types marked true in the vehicle scope file's `also_kept_column` judged as if they were in scope), `supply` stores the listed fields as not recorded and sums the rows that become identical. The model of a trailer or a caravan is free text typed at registration, and the dataset never reads it. Everything else about those rows is kept, so their counts stay askable. The scope is written into the ledger; a store written under another scope is refused until the history is supplied again.
nzta_dashboard.$max_month_change_comment: A month already in the last good build may differ from it by at most this share, unless the ledger records that month as replaced (the dashboard restates past months; a restatement is recorded, not silent).

statsnz_tpt.$comment: Stats NZ's table of new and ex-overseas motor vehicles registered by type, monthly (Infoshare TPT052601), exported by hand as CSV. A source of kind series: pipeline/series.py. Everything about the table is here and in the reference file named under catalogue: the title and footer the export must carry, the months' format, the columns (catalogue: one row per column header, in order) and what each is. The store holds a figure for each month and series; a `..` (figure not available) is never stored.
statsnz_tpt.origin: Stats NZ's Infoshare, table TPT052601 (Transport - TPT), exported as CSV and checked by `python -m pipeline supply`.
statsnz_tpt.title: New and Ex-Oseas Motor Vehicles Registered by Type (Monthly)
statsnz_tpt.$arithmetic_from_comment: From this month a total must equal the sum of its parts or the export is refused. Before it the disagreements are warnings: they are all in 1975-07, 1976-05, 1977-02, 1978-07, 1981-03, 1996-04 and 1997-08 in the export of 2026-11-14, and there are none from 1998-01.
statsnz_tpt.$max_month_change_comment: A month's total already in the last good build may not differ from it at all, unless the ledger records a revision of that month accepted since (--accept-revisions).
statsnz_tpt.attribution: This work is based on/includes Stats NZ's data which are licensed by Stats NZ for reuse under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence.

reconciliation.$comment: Every build sets figures that other organisations publish beside the same figures read from the files it is about to publish, and writes reconciliation.json (pipeline/reconcile.py, docs/CUBE_SCHEMA.md, D-149). What is compared is data: figures_file holds one row per published figure and sources_file one per organisation, both in reference_dir. A row past its own tolerance_pct warns, one line for each source. The hard limit stops the build, because separate counts agreeing with each other and not with ours in the same month, on the same side, mean our data is wrong, not theirs. A row is past its hard bound when ours is further from theirs than tolerance_multiple times the row's own tolerance, but never less than floor_pct, so a very tight tolerance cannot turn a gap of a few vehicles into a breach. A source is judged for one month by vehicles, not rows: the weight of a compared row is its published figure, and the source breaches on one side (ours below theirs, or above) when its rows past their hard bound on that side hold at least source_vehicle_share of the weight of all its compared rows that month. Rows on the other side do not cancel it. A total and its parts both count: it is a share of what the source published, not of vehicles. The build stops when, in one month, at least min_sources independent sources (the `independent` column of sources_file) breach on the same side and they are more than half of the independent sources that have any compared row that month. A month with compared rows from fewer than two independent sources cannot stop a build. One source restating its history, a source that cannot be read, and a month our data does not hold yet are not enough on their own. A single figure also stops the build, and one is enough (D-150): a compared row of an independent source whose figure_kind is in single_figure_limit.kinds, and whose own tolerance_pct is below gap_pct, stops it when ours is gap_pct percent or more from theirs, on either side (exactly gap_pct stops it), however few other sources or rows there are. A row of a listed kind whose tolerance_pct is gap_pct or more is exempt, because the row itself says ours cannot come that close, and must say why in known_difference. An empty kinds list switches the rule off. figure_kinds lists every kind a row of figures_file may state: a row with any other is refused when the file is read, so a misspelt kind cannot fall out of the rule unnoticed, and single_figure_limit.kinds may name only kinds it lists. A source can restate a figure it published earlier (D-153): the row holds the new figure in figure and the old one in restated_from, and a restatement of restatement_warn_pct percent or more of the earlier figure (exactly that counts) is warned about and listed on the status page, and the row is never better than warn; it does not stop the build. On such a row the single-figure limit stops the build only when ours is gap_pct or more from both the current figure and the earlier one. The hard limit above is unchanged. max_tolerance_pct is the largest tolerance a row may state; a larger one is a typing mistake.

events.$enum_columns_comment: The columns whose values must come from their enum in the schema table of enum_doc. The values are read from the table; this list makes a row that stops parsing as an enum abort the build instead of dropping its check.

register_archive.$comment: The whole register for each snapshot month, one row per vehicle, kept as one Parquet file in a private store outside git (pipeline/archive.py). It holds every field of pipeline/expected_schema.json except never_pulled: the chassis and engine numbers, which are never asked for. The first 11 characters of the VIN and the owner's postcode are kept in this private file only: neither is bound, built into the cube or published (D-076). The row id is pulled for paging and left out of the file.
register_archive.attribution: Motor Vehicle Register open data, NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi, licensed CC BY 4.0. One row per vehicle on the register at the snapshot date.

site_reader.$comment: What the site's Parquet reader can decode (src/lib/data.ts: its own pages for snappy and uncompressed, the zstd decoder it is given). Every Parquet file a build writes to public/data must be in one of these, which pipeline/tests/test_parquet_codecs.py checks; a codec added here needs its decoder in data.ts first, and tests/site/ checks the two agree.
